item.title: Server Infrastructure and Home Automation
item.description:
Status

Personal/In Development

General Description

Personal lab infrastructure configured on low-power hardware (Raspberry Pi / Linux node) to self-host local network services, automation routines, and sensor data ingestion.

Current Services

  • Pi-Hole
  • Unbound
  • Nginx
  • MQTT
  • Lightweight dashboard
  • Custom scripts

Architecture and Tools

  • Home Assistant: Central automation hub for device control and monitoring.
  • Docker: Containerized service isolation for local utilities and network tools. - Linux / Raspberry Pi: Low-power server running 24/7.

Focus

Local data privacy, system reliability, and automated alerts for home network metrics.

item.title: Bioimage Analysis Experiments with Cellpose
item.description:
Status

Experimental/Prototype

Overview

Personal computational biology experiments evaluating deep learning-based cell segmentation tools (Cellpose) for the quantitative analysis of confocal and fluorescence microscopy images.

Technical Scope

  • Python and Cellpose: Evaluation of pre-trained cell segmentation models on confocal microscopy images.
  • Image Processing: Batch feature extraction (cell area, signal intensity, cell count).
  • Jupyter Notebooks: Exploratory pipelines for data analysis and visualization.

Focus

Evaluating segmentation accuracy and automating cell counting workflows for bioimaging datasets.

item.title: Automation in a Mobile Environment with Termux
item.description:
Status

Unvalidated prototype

General Description

A custom command-line environment and script suite for Android devices leveraging Termux to enable lightweight background automation, remote task execution, and status checks for homelab servers and traditional home automation systems.

Technical Scope

  • Termux and POSIX Shell: Lightweight Linux environment running directly on mobile hardware.
  • Python and Bash: Background scripts, SSH key management, and API queries.
  • Remote Utilities: Quick status checks and emergency control scripts accessible from anywhere.

Approach

Repurposing mobile hardware as low-power, portable nodes for personal workflows.
